title: Thirty Years On Wednesday
subject: the hairdresser who has kept a standing hour for your mother for thirty years
caption: Retro soul cut live with a band. Hammond organ with the rotary speaker audible, a three-piece horn section playing tight punchy figures, bass guitar played with a dead flatwound tone sitting almost like an upright, drum kit recorded with a narrow room mic so it reads nearly mono, tambourine on the backbeat. Warm, narrow, mono-leaning mix with tape saturation and almost no vocal grid-editing. Rich female voice in a full chest register, delivered as a live take with slight pitch drift kept in, backing vocals in a loose trio. 98 BPM, E flat major. Warm and quietly astonished. No modern pop production, no autotune, no programmed drums, no synth, no key change.
lyrics:
[Intro - organ swell and horns]

[Verse 1]
Thirty years on Wednesday, ten o'clock, the same chair by the window
Donna knows my mother's head better than I know my own name
She knows which year was the hard one. She was there for it, with a comb.
She has never once asked about it. That's the whole gift.

[Chorus]
Thirty years on Wednesday
A woman who keeps a standing hour for my mother
No contract, no kin, no reason she has to
That's a kind of love nobody ever wrote a word for

[Verse 2]
Mama goes in tired and comes out taller
Doesn't matter what Donna did. Might be nothing. Might be everything.
Last month Donna's knees went bad, so Mama brings the chair now
Thirty years in, and the appointment just turned itself around

[Chorus]
Thirty years on Wednesday
A woman who keeps a standing hour for my mother
No contract, no kin, no reason she has to
That's a kind of love nobody ever found a word for

[Bridge - horns only]
I don't go to church
I drive my mother on Wednesdays
Close enough for me

[Outro - organ, fading]
Ten o'clock
Same chair by the window
